articles.title: 13 Books Like Harry Potter That Are Just as Magical to Read
articles.summary: Pick up your magic wand and get somewhere comfy for these next fantasy fiction reads like Harry Potter.
articles.body:
It's the perfect time to grab your trunk and check out of Hogwarts to move on to something new. If you don't plan on re-reading all seven books any time soon, there's nothing to fear as there are plenty of other brilliant books that will sate your appetite for fantastical storytelling. From magical school murder mystery novels to spell-teaching academies in the clouds, to low stakes fantasy to a boarding school for kids rejected from the mythical portals that once welcomed them; you'll find something to love in our list. So pick up your magic wand, settle into a comfy spot, and get ready to find some new favorite titles like Harry Potter worth reading in 2025 and beyond.

If you're looking for that feeling of being a new student at a magical academy, this is the perfect book for you. The Marvellers will make you feel like a little kid again, as Dhonielle Clayton guides us into the enchanting world of the Arcanum, a global magic school sitting high in the clouds. Ella is the school's first conjurer and she couldn't be more excited, but Arcanum isn't all that it's promised and there are secrets and mistrust behind the gilded doors. Clayton crafts a world you want nothing more than to join, but never shies away from the grim realities that would impact even the most magical of spaces. Ella is a dynamic lead and you'll come away from the Marvellers desperate to read more and rejoin Ella in her new magical world.

2. Percy Jackson & the Olympians by Rick Riordan

Rick Riordan's epic fantasy series has always been a great counterpoint / companion to the Boy Who Lived and is overall a fantastic coming-of-age story. Introducing readers to a world where the children of gods live among us, the first book follows Percy Jackson the son of Poseidon who must go on a dangerous journey to find a thief who has stolen Zeus' lightning bolts and clear his own name. These inclusive, thoughtful stories do a great job balancing the fantastical with the everyday featuring a hero with ADHD and Dyslexia and dealing with the sometimes hard realities of growing up. Riordan began writing these stories for his son, but the immersive, sprawling world he's created has become a favorite for readers around the globe and once you pick them up it's easy to see why.

You can check out our full guide to the Percy Jackson books in order or even check out the Percy Jackson series on Disney+ for more of this. The second season of the show has started on Disney+ as of December 2025.

Percy Jackson & the Olympians Paperback Boxed Set

3. Impossible Creatures by Katherine Rundell

Impossible Creatures is a fairly new series from author Katherine Rundell that has some serious Harry Potter vibes as a british children's fantasy novel. The story follows a young boy named Christopher who discovers a hidden archipelego of mythical creatues while visiting his grandfather. If you liked how well Harry Potter slowly introduced you to a hidden magical world through the perspective of a seemingly ordinary human, then this series is absolutely worth a try. There are only two books so far, but it has already been picked up by Disney for a live-action adaptation.

4. The Towar of Beggars (Stormfell Academy)

The Tower of Beggars started as a popular fantasy series in Germany before making its English translation debut this year. While it's not exactly like Harry Potter, the story features an orphan girl with a good heart that learns to survive with the help of unlikely friends. Here's what we said in our 8 out of 10 review of the book :

"The Tower of Beggars is a solid fantasy book that breaks from the usual magical school trope. Thanks to a very likeable protagonist and a gold-hungry pocket dragon, the story is hard to put down once you get started. Fans of Brandon Sanderson's Mistborn series and Harry Potter are likely to enjoy everything the first book in the Stormfell Academy series has to offer." - Jacob Kienlen

The Tower of Beggars: Stormfell Academy Book One

5. Eragon (The Inheritance Cycle) by Christopher Paolini

Although it doesn't include any sort of academy or school, The Inhertiance Cycle by Christopher Paolini is an excellent read to follow up on if you loved Harry Potter. The story is all about a young teen named Eragon who stumbles upon a dragon egg only to get swept up into a world of magic, danger, and dragons. With a total of four books in the series, you get to see the main character and his dragon grow up as they deal with a seemingly all-powerful malevolent enemy that seeks to destroy everything they love. It's a great young adult fantasy that falls somewhere between Harry Potter and the Lord of the Rings books .

If your favorite thing about visiting Hogwarts was the sumptuous feasts and visits to Hogsmede, then Legends & Lattes is the perfect pick for your next read. Travis Baldree's gorgeous cozy fantasy has taken the internet by storm and for good reason. This beautiful tale of an Orc giving up her warrior ways and starting a coffee shop is one of the most magical and fantastical stories of recent years. Filled with delicious baked goods, steaming hot drinks, and charming customers, this is a found family yarn that will fulfill your fantasy needs but won't give you anxiety as the stakes are always relatively low, and the violence of high fantasy is nowhere to be seen. Instead the pages are stuffed with fun banter, burgeoning romance, and baking. It's a great urban fantasy for teens or adults to dig into.

Aiden Thomas made a huge splash with this stunning debut about a trans boy who dreams of becoming a Brujo but accidentally summons the wrong ghost and has to deal with the fallout. Yadriel knows who he is and when his family struggles to accept his gender, he tries to prove them wrong with a spell, but instead of summoning his cousin, he ends up summoning the ghost of his school's notorious bad boy Julian. Left with no choice Yadriel has to help Julian come to terms with his fate and move on before he can get back to his normal life. Sweet, scary, and romantic this is a dark fantasy novel like no other that will keep you reading 'til the very last page.

One of the most innovative entries into the magical school canon, this collection of short stories are woven together to tell the story of the Galileo Academy for the Extraordinary that is torn apart by a murder. Over 18 chapters, 18 authors — Cam Montgomery, Darcie Little Badger, Hafsah Faizal, Jessica Lewis, Julian Winters, Karuna Riazi, Kat Cho, Kayla Whaley, Kwame Mbalia, L. L. McKinney, Marieke Nijkamp, Mason Deaver, Natasha Díaz, Preeti Chhibber, Randy Ribay, Tehlor Kay Mejia, Victoria Lee, and Yamile Saied Méndez — take on 18 students' perspectives for a bracing, subversive, and ultimately radical take on the magic school trope. Grimoire of the Grave Fates is the kind of thoughtful fantasy that we need much, much more of.

Murders are rife at magical schools, because that's exactly what occurs in Magic For Liars when a gruesome killing drags private detective Ivy Gamble back to the supernatural world that rejected her. While her sister Tabitha found success and ultimately a teaching job at The Osthorne Academy of Young Mages, Ivy was left in the cold and is barely scraping by as a PI when she's hired to solve a murder at the very place her estranged twin teaches. This contemporary twist on the classic magic school tale is witty, adult, and is set in a recognizably realistic world with a subtly magical twist. While the mystery will keep you guessing it's the intricate character work and relationships that will have you gripped throughout.

This beautiful collection of the first three stories in Seanan McGuire's Wayward Children is the perfect summer to fall read. McGuire's best selling novellas have been enchanting readers since the release of Every Heart a Doorway and now they're collected for the first time. Set against the backdrop of a school for kids who have been kicked out of portal worlds — think Alice in Wonderland or the Narnia books — the series begins with a murder mystery and never stops surprising. Filled with interesting complex kids, unbelievable worlds, and McGuire's engaging storytelling, these are some of the best fantasy stories of the last decade, so get your copy and get ready to fall in love and have your heartbroken as you explore what's through the door...

11. Sufficiently Advanced Magic by Andrew Rowe

The Arcane Ascension series from Andrew Rowe is a great option if you love reading about the inner workings of magic. The first few books in the series include a magic school setting that just feels magical. You also get a look into the professor's motivations and teachings through the eyes of the main character in a way that really builds up the academy vibe. The later books dive beyond school and into the larger fantasy world and politics, but it's all very well written. The story also has many elements from the popular progression fantasy genre that are more intriguing than the power scales in the Harry Potter universe.

Sufficiently Advanced Magic (Arcane Ascension)

The Empyrean series is a lot steamier than Harry Potter ever really got, but it has a lot of similar themes you'd find from the wizarding world. There's Dragons, a school, an underestimated main character, and magic. It has all of the elements of a good fantasy story that will scratch that Potter itch while also offering up some very graphic adult scenes . The author, Rebecca Yarros, blends sex with fantasy in this book in a way that has been blazing the path ahead for the romantasy genre. With the release of Onyx Storm earlier this year, the Fourth Wing books have been dominating the Kindle charts for 2025. The graphic content may make this book unsuitable for kids , but it's a great Harry Potter alternative for adults to read. This is arguably the best dragon school series of the modern era.

If you're interested in the romantasy aspect of Fourth Wing, you should also check out Alchemised . It was originally a Harry Potter fanfic that got adapted into it's own novel.

Another good Harry Potter alternative for adults is the Mistborn series. It doesn't feature a magical school, but you do get introduced to a very interesting world full of people with unique abilities. The story itself focuses on a young thief and and old legend as they work together to overthrow an evil empire. There are three books in the series, but it's a great entry point into Brandon Sanderson's Cosmere universe , which has more depth than even a fantasy world as big as Harry Potter.

For those who are already familiar with the popular Harry Potter fan-fiction Manacled, this book likely won't be surprised. This is essentially that same exact story with all of the Harry Potter-specific intellectual property removed. Alchemised is a dark romance novel about a prisoner who falls in love with her captor. As a romantasy, it's definitely meant more for adults than the younger generation. It has already been picked up for a movie adaptation , though we don't yet have the details of when production will begin.

Itching for more Hogwarts? Dive into the wizarding world alongside your friends with one of the best Harry Potter board games . You can also check out our list of the best movies like Harry Potter for a cinematic experience similar to the Harry Potter films . We've also found some of the overally best Harry Potter gifts available now.

Rosie Knight is a contributing freelancer for IGN covering everything from anime to comic books to kaiju to kids movies to horror flicks. She has over half a decade of experience in entertainment journalism with bylines at Nerdist, Den of Geek, Polygon, and more.

articles.title: This $79 controller brings features usually only found on those that cost twice as much.
articles.summary: The GameSir G7 Pro doesn’t cost nearly as much as other high-end controllers, but it brings everything to the table and largely succeeds.
articles.body:
A lot of high-end features are trickling down to more affordable game controllers these days, and that culminates in promising pieces of hardware like the GameSir G7 Pro controller, which combines tri-mode connectivity, TMR joysticks, fast poling rates and a whole lot more to become a serious threat for expensive controllers. The GameSir G7 Pro costs just $79, but is ready to rival the $179 Xbox Elite Wireless Series 2 controller and even the $199 Turtle Beach Stealth Ultra in many respects.

The GameSir G7 Pro looks a bit like a typical Xbox controller but with some unique aesthetic choices. It still has modest looks, but it’s also hiding some very interesting aspects. Behind its plain white faceplate and bland gray grips, it’s hiding a fully transparent panel that shows through to the circuit board and two of the four vibration motors. If you want the transparent style, you can readily remove each grip and/or the faceplate in any combination.

That’s just a small bit of the customization and flexibility that the G7 Pro brings to the table, too. The controller offers three D-Pad options. It has trigger locks. It has extra paddle buttons on the underside that also include physical lock switches. It can run wirelessly with a dedicated dongle or use a hardwired connection, and both support a 1,000Hz refresh rate. It can connect to mobile devices and more over Bluetooth. A special (removable) cable retainer can help brace the cable connection so it’s less likely to get damaged or come unplugged during play. And that’s all before getting into the software customizations.

You can slot GameSir’s USB-A transmitter dongle directly into a PC for wireless gaming. A charging dock is also included in the package, and it has a compartment for the transmitter dongle, so you can combine them at your desk for simple connectivity and charging in one. The charging dock is nothing special, offering a basic stand for the controller with pogo pins akin to what we’ve seen from similar 8BitDo controllers. There’s a helpful light on the dock to confirm when the controller is charging so you won’t come back to find it dead.

The hardware of the controller itself is very respectable. GameSir chucked mushy membrane switches and went all out. The ABXY and D-Pad get clicky micro switches like you’d find in a gaming mouse or high-end controller like the Turtle Beach Stealth Ultra. The triggers get nuanced Hall Effect sensors with short-throw trigger locks that convert them to micro switches as well. The shoulder buttons feel basic, but GameSir fit an extra set of custom shoulder buttons next to them, and those get the clicky micro switches as well. The two custom underside buttons don’t feel like micro switches, but even they are satisfyingly clicky. And the joysticks use TMR tech for accuracy and consistency that shouldn’t lead to stick drift in the long term.

For responsiveness, the controller also supports a 1,000Hz polling rate on PC whether using a wired or wireless connection (not Bluetooth though).

While most of the controller is hard plastic, the handles and joysticks get rubberized material with a diamond-pattern texture. This proves good for grip, though can get a bit grimy over time.

The GameSir G7 Pro has multiple apps. There’s one for mobile that doesn’t do anything beyond letting you test that each input is functioning. The GameSir Nexus app for PC is what you need to really get into the nitty gritty customization. In the app, you can swap out button assignments, adjust response curves and behavior for the triggers and joysticks, set up and tune gyro controls, and customize the four vibration motors. You can also set up four different profiles.

As powerful as the app is, it’s not without its faults. It frequently likes to disconnect from the controller, kicking you back to the landing page and taking a few seconds to get back into customization. This back-and-forth hand-off also makes it that much slower to make adjustments, test them in a game, and then switch back to tweak them. A lot of things aren’t well explained in the app either, so figuring out what you’ve changed can sometimes be a matter of guess-and-check.

Even without the app, there is some customization available. The controller supports on-the-fly button mapping for its four extra buttons. This entails simply long-pressing the M button and a desired extra button simultaneously then pressing the button you want mapped to it.

While it’s a shame GameSir doesn’t offer all this customization for the mobile app as well, settings adjusted on PC can carry over to mobile as well. For instance, I set up the gyroscope for aiming behavior in the PC app, and then connected to mobile over Bluetooth and saw the gyro continue to operate in this manner.

The GameSir G7 Pro provides an excellent gaming experience. Throughout my testing, it has left little to be desired. Through my sweatiest boss fights in Hollow Knight, the grips helped me keep a good hold on the controller. The microswitches for most of the buttons are wonderful for fast, responsive gaming, and every input registers with a snap. The ability to turn the analog triggers into short-throw microswitches also helps out big time for responsiveness, letting me dash in an instant in Hollow Knight while avoiding the extra strain of repeatedly pulling the trigger all the way.

The controller handles nuanced input well, too. The joysticks register subtle movements accurately, and the triggers can swap from snappy to standard analog triggers and enable more precise control. Running about in Battlefield 6, the controller was an accurate input tool, albeit not quite at mouse levels. The option to enable the gyroscope helped in some circumstances, though I could never get it to work perfectly. It tended to be a little jerky when emulating a controller input. When it emulated a mouse input, it was far more responsive and accurate, but it was also prone to very sudden, unpredictable camera movements if I touched the right joystick at all while aiming. This made it generally unreliable. Fortunately, for anyone who’s already great at joystick aim, the controller holds up well. The joysticks have grippy tops that can get a little grimey after a bit of use, but it’s not hard to clean

The G7 Pro’s combination of four rumble motors provide both powerful and subtle vibration that adds some extra dimension to games. The headset jack also provides convenient wireless connectivity for headphones and quick methods for adjusting chat and game volume balance (on Xbox) and muting your microphone.

Throughout testing, the wireless connection has been rock solid. While gaming, I’ve never experienced a drop-out even in environments with lots of radio interference. The 1,200mAh battery has also proven long-lasting. It likely helps that there’s no display or RGB lighting on the controller. Regardless, I was readily getting GameSir’s estimated 10-hour battery life. Though unless you’re playing marathon sessions, that battery life can be almost irrelevant, as the charging dock makes it easy to always have the controller topped up after gaming sessions.

articles.title: Labor Day Sales Are Now Live — Here's Where You Can Find Deals Today
articles.body:
Labor Day weekend is coming up, and for all of the Americans who don't work retail, that likely means a nice and long three-day weekend. It also means there are already plenty of Labor Day sales to check out.

As far as discounts go, Labor Day sales are not nearly as good as Black Friday or Prime Day. You probably aren't going to find many rock-bottom prices on anything, but there are still some good deals to be had if you're trying to save money.

For those just looking to do some general shopping, I've picked out the overall best sales happening at major retailers right now. If you're shopping for something specific, jump to the full list of sales by category .

Amazon is the best place to shop during sales events because it often matches prices everywhere else. As the largest online retailer, it has an advantage; a generally massive stock of everything. If one store discounts something popular, Amazon can adapt its pricing on the fly.

As for what's worth buying at Amazon during this time of year, your best bet is out-of-season gear. This includes outoor clothing, sporting goods, and shoes. You can also find some decent prices on electronics like Fire TV sticks and speakers if you don't want to wait for Black Friday. And while there aren't any deals on Amazon's Kindle devices so far this year, there are some solid discounts at the Kindle Store .

Best Buy has had a big month of savings so far, having just wrapped up its big 60th Anniversary sale . The Best Buy Labor Day sale is pretty much a continuation of those discounts and is generally the best place to find tech deals right now .

Some of the best things to buy at Best Buy include TVs, laptops, monitors, soundbars, and major appliances. For gamers, there are also deals on refurbished PS5 consoles, which is really the way to go in 2026 . And while it isn't tech-related, Best Buy is also having a sale on MTG cards this week.

The Barnes & Noble Book Haul sale has been going on since August, but it's still worth checking out if you haven't already. The discounts are available online or in-person at Barnes & Noble locations near you. The sale includes up to 50% off hardcovers books, 25% off LEGO sets, and some discounts on B&N-exclusive editions.

Amazon has already price-matched many of the best book deals at Barnes & Noble, so the deals on exclusive hardcover editions are what I'd recommend checking out first if you're looking for deals you won't find elsewhere. There are also some LEGO Wednesday set deals here that have yet to be matched.

Target's Labor Day sale has many of the same deals you'll find at Best Buy, Amazon, or Walmart, but with a few extra things thrown in. The big highlight is that Target has some pretty good deals on groceries .

These Labor Day sales are also in stores if you prefer to do your shopping in person. Seeing as it's back-to-school season, some of the best things to buy from Target right now are back-to-school things. You may want to browse online before heading to the store to pick up those supplies. I went to pick out a new lunch pale for my son at the Target closest to me last weekend and stock was pretty much wiped out.

Note : This list only includes retailers that explicitly have a Labor Day sale event going on right now. We'll be updating this list as more sales go live this week.

Jacob Kienlen is a Senior Audience Development Strategist and Writer for IGN. Born and raised in Portland, Oregon, he has considered the Northwest his home for his entire life. With a bachelor's degree in communication and 10 years of professional writing experience, his expertise is spread across a variety of different pop culture topics -- from TV series to books and the latest LEGO sets .

articles.title: IGN Australia and Chupa Chups to Host a Retro Gaming ‘Fun House’ Activation at Westfield Parramatta This October
articles.summary: IGN Australia and Chupa Chups to Host a Retro Gaming ‘Fun House’ Activation at Westfield Parramatta This October
articles.body:
Looking for some free fun October 1 to 4? Chupa Chups is teaming up with IGN Australia and Westfield Parramatta for four days of free gaming goodness this October school holidays.

We're calling it the “ Chupa Chups Forever Fun House” - and Aussie IGNers are invited to come check out our 90s family dream home: four decorated rooms, loads of consoles and games, free Chupa Chups lollies and daily prize giveaways!

Doors open as soon as Westfield does - and it lasts all day until close, so come along and check it out. Did we mention it’s free?

When: Thursday, October 1: 9:30 AM – 9:00 PM Friday, October 2: 9:30 AM – 6:00 PM Saturday, October 3: 9:00 AM – 6:00 PM Sunday, October 4: 10:00 AM – 6:00 PM

Where: Westfield Parramatta, NSW, L2 Centre Court, Opposite Uniqlo

So what’s on show? We’ll have instant multiplayer party-makers like Mario Kart World, Super Smash Bros Ultimate and Minecraft Dungeons II.

Plus, we’ll have a few surprise titles throughout the week - so be sure to come back to the Chupa Chups Forever Fun House with your family and friends later on and flex your gaming prowess.

We’re also giving away a custom, one-off Chupa Chups Gaming PC by Aftershock! This beast is going to be showcased in the Fun House for one lucky winner to take home.

As if that’s not enough, you could also win a Xbox Series X, a PS5, a Switch 2 just by playing in the Fun House!

Entry's easy. Just scan a QR code at the event or head to Gleam.io, and follow IGN, Chupa Chups and Westfield on social for extra entries. Full details will be announced soon. Australian residents only, T&Cs apply. Full event details drop soon, so follow IGN AU on Facebook and Instagram if you’re not already!

Stay tuned for more info and announcements in the coming weeks!

articles.title: The Studio Behind Hit New Star Wars Game Zero Company Quietly Furloughed 'Most' Staff Just Before Launch
articles.summary: Bit Reactor, the studio behind Star Wars Zero Company, furloughed the majority of its staff just before the game launched.
articles.body:
Bit Reactor, the studio behind Star Wars Zero Company , furloughed the majority of its staff just before the game launched.

Critically praised and currently a bestseller on Steam, Star Wars Zero Company looked to have had a brilliant launch — though the celebrations have now been marred by word of what has happened to the people who made it.

A Game File report has now highlighted comments made by Zachariah Scott, a former Bit Reactor employee, who claimed the company was "concealing the fact that the team was furloughed weeks ago" — while its CEO Greg Foertsch was busy at Gamescom last week talking about the team's next game.

While Bit Reactor has since confirmed to Game File many of its staff are now on furlough, the exact numbers of people involved are unclear. The report's suggestion is that 80% of the studio have currently been placed on leave without pay, leaving behind a small number of staff to deal with any post-launch bugs. It's believed that Bit Reactor ran out of money to pay employees shortly before launch, despite hopes of landing another game deal, and a push to keep costs down with "austerity".

The furlough has come to light as part of messy legal action between Bit Reactor's former COO, Alison Kelly, and Foertsch. Kelly, another company co-founder, alleges she was pushed out of Bit Reactor by Foertsch and left without compensation for her stake. Foertsch has denied this and countersued, with a trial now set for early 2027.

One interesting part of all this is a claim that Zero Company ended up being made due to Kelly getting the project in front of the late Respawn and EA executive Zince Zampella, who initially considered the idea for a Titanfall spinoff, before suggesting it switch to being based around the Star Wars license instead.

Whether Star Wars Zero Company's success can salvage the studio and its team remains to be seen, and Bit Reactor has made no comment on how well the game needs to perform commercially in order to reinstate its staff.

"Star Wars Zero Company is an excellent tactical game that does a fantastic job of slathering on the same cinematic look and feel we saw in Respawn's Star Wars Jedi games," we wrote in IGN's Star Wars Zero Company review , which returned a 9/10, "incorporating strong characters and a storyline that's refreshingly centered on non-Force users and a non-traditional villain."

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

articles.title: After Being Ditched by Xbox, Double Fine Says It'll Make Brütal Legend 2 If Its Amnesia Fortnight 2026 Kickstarter Raises an Impossible-Sounding $100 Million
articles.summary: Psychonauts and Costume Quest maker Double Fine has launched its new game development Kickstarter project after cutting ties with Xbox, and says it'll make Brütal Legend 2 if it raises an impossible-sounding $100 million.
articles.body:
Psychonauts and Costume Quest maker Double Fine has launched its new game development Kickstarter project after cutting ties with Xbox, and says it'll make Brütal Legend 2 if it raises an impossible-sounding $100 million.

Double Fine is crowdfunding support for its new game jam on Kickstarter, the platform it previously used to successfully fund Broken Age, long before its recently-concluded stint as an Xbox-owned studio, and subsequent layoffs affecting 25% of its team .

With the Microsoft money pipe now severed, the maker of recent titles such as Kiln and Keeper must now fund its own experimental indie projects. And so, once again, it is holding a two-week stint of creating a series of bizarre prototypes, which fans of the company can choose to vote on and support.

At the time of writing, Double Fine's crowdfunding campaign has raised just over $275,000 of its current $400,000 goal, with 29 days still to go. It remains to be seen what further stretch goals will be added to the project as its progress continues, though the company has already promised it will develop a Brütal Legend sequel should it hit $100 million.

Now, to be clear, there is no realistic chance of this Kickstarter hitting $100 million, which begs the question of why Double Fine is teasing a follow-up to its beloved Jack Black-fronted real-time strategy title from 2009. Is this just a pipe dream, dangled in front of fans without likelihood of it occuring?

A year ago, Double Fine stated it had multiple projects in the works and that none of them were sequels . But this was before the company split from Microsoft, and it's reasonable to assume that plans have changed significantly since. Indeed, Double Fine has now clarified it is still working on larger game projects in the background, while the Amnesia Fortnight crowdfunder pays for the team's immediate future. Perhaps Brütal Legend 2 is one such larger project? It did depart Xbox with the rights to its game back catalog intact , after all.

We are still working on bigger games! This is to help keep us open while we seek funding for those larger projects, and also for the team to have fun with one of our favorite traditions after a very long, tough summer. 🫶🏼 — Double Fine Productions (@DoubleFine) August 31, 2026

We are still working on bigger games! This is to help keep us open while we seek funding for those larger projects, and also for the team to have fun with one of our favorite traditions after a very long, tough summer. 🫶🏼

In the meantime, you can browse pitch videos for more than 25 game prototypes via the Double Fine Kickstarter page, listed in full below, and pledge your support to then vote on which gets turned into an actual (albeit small) game. Which of these sounds worthy to you?

Architactics, a small scale tactical city builder where your structures can move like giant robots and fight back against environmental monsters

Astro Slam Intergalactic Pro Wrestling, a deck builder with tactical elements and story-driven branching paths

Bard Crawl, an online co-op adventure where a bar crawl with up to three friends shifts into a fantasy dungeon crawler

Brouroboros, a local multiplayer party game where each player controls a snake head on a shared body

Centauride, a 2v2 game where you scavenge, build and race a mechanical centaur

Cosmic Bonsai, a horticulture-inspired astronomical pseudo-simulation game

Dragons, Gels, and Bear-Owls, Oh My!, a chaotic, co-op survival game where you take care of magical beasts via mini-games

Echo, a music-based multiplayer 2D platformer, where your goal is to perform a short tune through parkour

Emergency Foley Artist, a party game where you create silly cartoon soundtracks

Fermi's Playground, tweak the laws of nature to shift the odds of habitable worlds and run the simulation to see what a galaxy of explorers requires

Friendslap, a satisfyingly silly and slap-tastic multiplayer arena

Golem Hero, a roguelite mix between Dynasty Warriors and Castle Crashers

Insolation, a survival game where you pilot an agile spider-bot to find and protect the last few plant species alive

Lesbian Sled Death, a four-player, jet-powered, full-contact Rocket Sled Derby racing game

Lucid Gardening, where you cultivate a supernatural garden of mysterious plants and animals

Mochimochi Line Dancer, a fast-paced Mochi-collecting game where you build the longest and wiggliest line dance before time runs out

Muscle Madness, a four-player creatine-fuelled race to see who's the swolest of them all

Plot Armor, a turn-based RPG/visual novel combo in which your narrative choices in the latter affect your character's performance in the former

Quokk 'n Roll, a play with your friends co-op escape gameReluctance, an arena shooter that bends its genre according to player action

R.U.N, a third-person action platformer where players must flee a mysterious force, making quick decisions to find the best path forward

Super Power Performance Evaluation, a co-operative action puzzler where you use randomly assigned superpowers to perform heroic feats

Tonight We Feast, a chaotic co-op caper about a fox, raccoon and pigeon trying to score a meal for the night in the big city

Tractor Takedown, a four-player local battle game where players drive hotrod tractors to stop data center construction

Uprise, a kite-flying high-speed platformer where you build and fly kits to rise up against a mysterious invading force

Virtual Pet Manifesto, a social idle game where you and your friends are virtual pets

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

articles.title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, God of War Laufey, and Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet: What to Expect From PlayStation’s State of Play September 2026
articles.summary:
Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, God of War Laufey, and Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet: 

Here's what to expect from Thursday's PlayStation State of Play streams.
articles.body:
Sony is returning with not just one, but two State of Play streams on September 3rd at 6am PT / 9am ET / 3:00pm CEST / 10:00pm JST , so get ready for a whole host of new PS5 game announcements, fresh looks at gameplay, and maybe even some other surprises. So far, Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is the only game we know will be shown, with an extended look at its vast world teased, but other "updates and announcements from PlayStation Studios and third-party partners" are promised. So, what could we see?

Well, we’ve got double the chance to see things this year, with a second showcase to follow directly after, focusing on studios from Japan and Asia. For context, last year’s equivalent stream gave us a gameplay trailer for Marvel’s Wolverine that included a release window reveal, a release date for Housemarque’s Saros, and a first look at Battlefield 6’s campaign. But what can we expect to see this year? Well, let’s get stuck in and look at exactly that.

Marvel’s Wolverine could make one final State of Play appearance ahead of its imminent September 15 release. Excitement levels are already high for this one, but I guess one more trailer or sneak peek can’t hurt.

Revealed at PlayStation’s June State of Play , God of War Laufey, is scheduled to arrive in February of 2027, which is creeping up on us quickly. So far, we’ve only seen that extended gameplay slice that came alongside its unveiling, so another look at it would be more than welcome. There are many directions that a potential trailer could take us, whether it be a deeper dive into the story, world, and characters we’ll meet on Faye’s journey, or a showcase of how differently she’ll perform in combat compared to her husband, Kratos. Either way, we can’t wait to see more.

Is it finally time for Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet to reemerge? It’s been over 18 months since the reveal of Naughty Dog’s latest, with that one trailer still our only glimpse of it. Some gameplay would be lovely, and if we’re dreaming, some sort of release date window would be very much appreciated, too. This week, we got the news that the shooting of its performance capture has been completed , alongside a social post from the studio that read “Cannot wait to show you their incredible work when the time is right!” Could that time be Thursday?

Housemarque only recently gave us Saros in April , but that doesn’t necessarily mean we won’t be seeing it here. After all, the studio’s previous game, Returnal, gave us a fair amount of post-launch additions, including co-op play and the endless Tower of Sisyphus mode. Could we see something similar come to Saros? The Finnish studio has already been in the news this week, following the departure of co-founder Ilari Kuittinen , who had been with the company for 31 years. One PlayStation Studios game we can probably expect to see DLC for is Ghost of Yotei, whose Echoes of Sekigahara story expansion drops alongside a new roguelike mode on October 1.

It feels a little too early to see what the third part of Guerrilla Games’ Horizon trilogy is, with reports suggesting it’s still many years away. And it seems as if we’ll be waiting a while to see anything from that universe, as Horizon: Hunter’s Gathering has reportedly been rebooted internally due to negative feedback from playtests. Could we ever see this live-service multiplayer spin-off again? With Halloween looming on the horizon, though, perhaps it’s time to get another look at what Until Dawn 2 may have in store for us.

As for other PlayStation studios, we still don’t know what a lot of them are working on. It’s fair to assume Polyphony is developing another Gran Turismo, and with it being over four years since the last, could we see Gran Turismo 8 pop up on the 3rd? 2027 marks 30 years for the series, so it seems like a nice time for another dose of sim-racing action if you ask me. It’s also been a long time since we’ve heard from LittleBigPlanet and Dreams creators Media Molecule , Days Gone developers Bend , and whatever is happening with Haven’s Fairgames — could it be rebranding to Break In? We’ll take hearing from any of these studios as a win.

And then there are the PS5 exclusives that are being made outside of Sony’s first-party structure, such as Phantom Blade Zero. The S-Game-developed action game looks more impressive each and every time we see new gameplay, and we certainly wouldn’t say no to another peek here, despite it receiving its own dedicated State of Play just a couple of weeks ago. Set for an October 28 release, it certainly makes sense for it to show up in some capacity during one of the two streams.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls has been received well — on console at least — following its recent August 6 release, so could developer Arc System Works be looking to keep that momentum going with a look at who will be joining the roster next? Dataminers uncovered five possible DLC characters a few weeks back, so could we see one of them pop up here?

Another PS5 exclusive, 4:Loop, staged a beta earlier in the year, suggesting that maybe it isn’t a million miles away from a release date either. The co-op shooter from JJ Abrams’ Bad Robot Studios, directed by Left4Dead’s Mike Booth, will be looking to turn around Sony’s multiplayer woes.

I’m by no means guaranteeing anything, but there is a tiny chance we’ll actually see GTA 6 at the first of the two State of Plays. Following its expansive extended look last week, a small follow-up here wouldn’t be beyond the realm of belief. Perhaps a look at how Rockstar’s latest will perform on PS5 Pro?

What we do know, is that part three of Square Enix's FF7 remake project, Final Fantasy 7 Revelation will end the first of the two showcases, with an extended look into its world promised. Speaking of Square...could we get a visit from Sora, Mickey, and friends as Kingdom Hearts 4 continues to steadily reveal what will be in store for the action RPG?

Revealed in February, Saber Interactive’s John Wick game was certainly a surprise. Some gameplay of this Keanu Reeves-starring prequel to the movies would be a treat. At the same State of Play, Konami’s first mainline Castlevania game in 17 years was announced, with Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse returning to its 2D action roots. With a long PlayStation lineage tied to the series, we wouldn’t be shocked to see it again. Two other games set to come out soon are Control Resonant and Star Wars: Galactic Racer, and could make a reappearance.

Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis is a remake of the original Lara Croft adventure, and, seeing as how important that game was for the original PlayStation, a State of Play would be a logical place for more of it to be shown off. Another series tied to Sony history is Resident Evil . Could it be time for another look at Resident Evil: Veronica ?

As if two Marvel games weren’t enough, there’s also a chance we’ll see Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra, which has been indefinitely delayed “beyond early 2026. ” If this really is Captain America and Black Panther in an Uncharted-like action-adventure from Amy Hennig, then a look at gameplay would be much welcomed. And then there’s Project Windless, a new action-adventure game starring a sword-wielding seven-foot chicken from PUBG publishers, Krafton . Now isn’t the time for me to fully go into details of the nightmares I used to have as a child about being chased by a giant chicken man, but I won’t lie to you, I’m both excited for and terrified of this game in equal measure.

So, that’s everything to expect from September 3rd’s two State of Play streams. There will, we hope, be plenty of surprises, though. What game are you most excited to see more of? Let us know in the comments below.

Simon Cardy is a Senior Editor at IGN who can mainly be found skulking around open world games, indulging in Korean cinema, or despairing at the state of Tottenham Hotspur and the New York Jets. Follow him on Bluesky at @cardy.bsky.social .

articles.title: 'I Don't Think There's Any Plan': Kit Harington Gives Disappointing Update on His Marvel Future as Black Knight
articles.summary: Game of Thrones star Kit Harrington has given a disappointing update on the future of his Marvel character Dane Whitman, better known as Black Knight.
articles.body:
Game of Thrones star Kit Harington has given a disappointing update on the future of his Marvel character Dane Whitman, better known as Black Knight.

Harrington joined the MCU as part of an extraordinarily starry cast in the 2021 sci-fi blockbuster Eternals . But despite Eternal's end credits promising that its superhero team would return, no mention has been made of the characters since, following the film's poor critical and commercial performance.

Marvel boss Kevin Feige admitted back in 2022 that there are no plans for an Eternals 2 at the current time, and there's been zero word to suggest this has changed in the meantime. But perhaps more than any other character in the Eternals, fans have long held onto hope that Harington could still reprise his role someday — if not in a full sequel then perhaps in another project.

Every Loose End in the Marvel Cinematic Universe

Fans have long wanted Marvel to announce a Midnight Sons team-up movie, and still hold hope one may materialize eventually. Not only could Harington return without the rest of the Eternals, it would also be a neat place to feature Ryan Gosling's Ghost Rider following his introduction. And hey, Mahershala Ali's Blade could appear there too!

But, for now at least, Harrington has suggested this is not on the cards. Talking to Movie Web , the actor said he wasn't aware of any invitation to rejoin the Marvel universe.

"I'd love to [return]," Harington began. "I don't think there's any plan to. I hate to break it to you.

"I think he's a wicked character," he continued. "There's a part of him, that whole Ebony Blade stuff, where the more he kills the worse he gets, the more addicted. I think he's such a great parable of addiction. I think he's someone who starts good and goes bad. But we'll see, I don't know if there's any plan."

Marvel has its next few years fully mapped out, with Avengers: Doomsday this December, and Avengers: Secret Wars due in December 2027. The following year sees Marvel's next phase kick off in style, with X-Men, Ghost Rider and Black Panther 3. As for Harington himself, the actor previously passed on the chance to return as Jon Snow in a rather depressing-sounding Game of Thrones sequel series . Last month, it was confirmed he will play Gilderoy Lockhart in HBO's upcoming Harry Potter series , replacing Superman star Nicholas Hoult.
